title: [Project] QR Code Generator
summary: Capstone for the Node section: a command-line program that asks for a URL with the inquirer package, turns it into a PNG QR code with qr-image, and saves the URL to a text file with the native fs module. The walkthrough doubles as practice at reading package documentation and converting CommonJS examples to ES module imports.

concepts.heading: Project overview and packages
points: A QR code is a 2D barcode that a phone camera scans to open a URL.
inquirer collects typed input from the terminal. qr-image generates QR images (PNG by default). fs (native) writes files.
Spelling matters: inquirer is easy to misspell, and qr-image has a hyphen, not an underscore. Verify names on npmjs.com before installing.
Install both in one command: npm i inquirer qr-image. The install reported about 50 packages because each package brings its own dependencies into node_modules; they are small.
(Extra) fs is a built-in module and needs no install; the reference repo's package.json lists an "fs" security placeholder package, which is unnecessary.

concepts.heading: Preparing package.json for ES modules
points: The project had no full package.json, which shows npm init -y can be run any time, even after installing packages; -y accepts all defaults.
Add "type": "module" so import syntax works. Without it Node reports that import cannot be used outside a module.
(Extra) Optionally fill in the author field.

concepts.heading: Step 1: get user input with inquirer
points: The docs example calls inquirer.prompt([...questions]) which returns a promise. .then receives an answers object; .catch handles errors.

Each question is an object. message is the text shown to the user; name is the key under which the answer is stored. Many other options exist and are optional. Several questions can be passed in the array.
Question used: { message: "Type in your URL", name: "URL" }.
First log answers to see its shape: an object such as { URL: "www.google.com" }. Then read answers.URL into a const url.
Run from the project folder with node index.js. (Extra) The catch block's error.isTtyError check distinguishes a terminal that cannot show prompts from other failures.

concepts.heading: Step 2: create the QR image with qr-image
points: The docs example uses require. It must be converted: import qr from "qr-image" and import fs from "fs". CommonJS require and ESM import cannot be mixed in one file.
qr.image(text, options) returns a readable stream. The options object (type, size, margin and so on) is optional; the default type is PNG, so it can be omitted.
Pipe the stream into a file: qr_svg.pipe(fs.createWriteStream("qr_img.png")). This writes the PNG into the project folder.
Test with a full URL including https:// and scan the result with a phone to confirm it opens the right site.
(Extra) The qr-image README example passes { type: 'svg' } and names its variable qr_svg; the lecture drops the type option so the output is PNG (the default), and the variable name has no effect.

concepts.heading: Step 3: save the URL with fs.writeFile
points: Call fs.writeFile("URL.txt", url, callback) inside the same .then block, after the image code.
The callback receives err; throw it if present, otherwise log a confirmation message.
Final outcome of one run: a qr_img.png and a URL.txt containing the typed text in the project folder.

concepts.heading: Workflow lessons
points: Read each package's documentation first, paste its example, then adapt it. The qr-image source lives in node_modules/qr-image/lib, which can be browsed to see what is exported.
Typing the import line before using a name lets the editor autocomplete.
Getting stuck and digging through docs is the expected part of the process. Next section: Express.

task.name: QR Code Generator
task.starting_point: index.js with a comment block listing three TODOs, an empty or partial package.json.
task.goal: Running node index.js asks for a URL, writes a QR code PNG for it and a text file containing the URL.
steps: Install inquirer and qr-image with npm i (check spelling on npmjs.com).
Import inquirer and call inquirer.prompt with one question object that has message and name.
In .then, read answers.URL into a const.
Import qr from qr-image; create the image with qr.image(url) and pipe it to fs.createWriteStream("qr_img.png").
Import fs and call fs.writeFile to save the URL to URL.txt, with an error-throwing callback.
Run it, enter a full https URL, then scan the PNG with a phone to check it.
task.expected_result: After entering e.g. https://www.google.com, the folder contains qr_img.png (scans to that URL) and URL.txt holding the same text.

pitfalls: Misspelling the package names (inquirer, qr-image with a hyphen).
Forgetting "type": "module", which causes the import error.
Leaving require() lines from the docs alongside import statements.
Typing a URL without https:// makes a QR code phones may treat as plain text.
Running node from the wrong folder so files land elsewhere.

The reference repo's index.js differs slightly from the lecture: it saves to link.txt rather than URL.txt and logs placeholder 'Error 1/2' messages; its package.json also lists an unnecessary "fs" placeholder dependency and the student's name as author (ignore both).

gaps_and_ideas: Proposed lesson 'Node QR generator': blurb about combining two npm packages and fs. Tasks: 1) install packages and set type module, 2) prompt for a URL and log answers, 3) create the PNG, 4) write URL.txt, 5) extend with a second question for the file name.
Starter code: index.js containing only the TODO comment block and import lines.
Interactive demo idea: simulated terminal prompt that takes a URL, draws a QR code in a canvas and shows the two output files appearing in a mock file tree.
Stretch tasks: add a size option to qr.image, validate the URL, use the promise form fs.promises.writeFile.
